name: Staffhaus-Wiese
beschreibung:
Overview

The Staffhaus-Wiese is one of a total of ten camp sites of the Tiroler Pfadfinderzentrum Igls (TPZ), the province association of the Tyrolean Scouts' own centre. The site is located in the Innsbruck district of Igls at Heiligwasserwiese 5 (postcode 6080). It is operated by the province association, which is part of Pfadfinder und Pfadfinderinnen Österreichs (PPÖ).

The centre primarily hosts scout groups but is equally open to other youth groups, clubs and events from Austria and abroad. The individual meadows vary in size and are suitable for different group sizes; the Staffhaus-Wiese lies next to the Staffhaus that gives it its name. For camping guests, outdoor sanitary facilities are available: twelve washbasins for washing dishes, eight showers and four separately lockable washrooms with two to three toilets and one lockable shower each. Eight lockable refrigerators can be rented.

The centre also includes the main house with space for 74 people – 43 beds in seven rooms on the first and 31 beds in six rooms on the second floor. Each floor has two wash and shower rooms as well as two separate toilets; on the first floor there is also a seminar room for around 30 people. On the ground floor are the dining hall and catering kitchen, in the basement a large multipurpose room, a gymnastics and bouldering room and a lounge with table football. For camps, fire bowls, grid grates and bricks, table and beer bench sets as well as building materials for camp structures can be borrowed, among other things.

History/Background

The Tyrolean scout movement looks back on more than a hundred years of history: in 1914 Emmerich Teuber, a veteran of the Tiroler Kaiserjäger, gave a much-noted lecture in Innsbruck on 13 January, as a result of which four scout groups were formed at the commercial academy in May 1914. The province association celebrated its 111th anniversary in 2025 (1914–2025) and is part of Pfadfinder und Pfadfinderinnen Österreichs. According to the official website, the centre's Staffhaus is currently unavailable due to extensive renovation work; among other things, it is to be made barrier-free.

Getting there

The Tiroler Pfadfinderzentrum Igls is located at Heiligwasserwiese 5 in 6080 Innsbruck/Igls, in the south of Innsbruck. According to the official notice, groups must generally organise their own travel. Reliable information on public transport or parking is not published on the centre's website; concrete routes are therefore best clarified directly at the time of booking. Booking is done via the booking form on the website, which is connected to the scoutbooking portal; if you have any questions, the team is available at tpz-buchung@pfadis.tirol.

Tips

Some things you need to bring yourself: according to the centre, toilet paper, hand soap, washing-up liquid, sponges and tea towels are not provided. In the main house, bed linen must be brought yourself or rented for a fee; a fitted sheet must be pulled over the mattress hygiene covers. Indoor shoes are compulsory in the house (no shoes indoors), smoking is only permitted in the designated area on the terrace, and waste separation is expressly requested. For the camp site, construction timber, a barbecue barrel, waste stands and sanitary facilities can be used; beer bench sets and refrigerators can be rented for an extra charge. Please also note that the sanitary facilities can only be reached via a sloping path and are not barrier-free.

Best time to travel

The centre does not name a fixed, officially published season; use and availability depend on group bookings and the weather. According to the website, the main house can also be used in winter and then offers storage facilities for skis and ski boots, while camping on the meadows depends on the weather. If you want to camp in the warm months, you should clarify the date and conditions with the administration early on.
